newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RTRS-Telecom Q1 net profit on forecast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Telecom Q1 net profit on forecast.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand on Tuesday reported first quarter earnings of NZ$188.0 million against the year ago profit of $177.1 million.
Analysts had forecast a result within $5 million of $190 million.
The phone utility, controlled a quarter each by Bell Atlantic and Ameritech, paid a 10.5 cents per share dividend against 9.5 cents a year ago.
The dividend amounts to 100.7 percent of earnings. Due to seasonal factors, earnings are not distributed evenly during the year.
The 1997/98 result does not include operating results for Telecom's loss-making Australian unit, Pacific Star, which have already been provided for and is being wound down.
The 1996/97 result included Pacific Star's $11.5 million operating loss.
Revenue in the quarter rose by 9.6 percent, while normalised revenue was up 7 percent. The company said volume growth in core services continued to be strong, offsetting price reductions.

Operating expenses increased by $51.9 million, 12.1 percent, largely because of higher depreciation, personnel costS and sales costs. Cost of sales were up 19.6 percent when adjusted for an accounting change.
Telecom said the result was achieved against a background of a sluggish economy where GDP fell 0.5 percent in the March quarter.
It said it expected competition to remain intense with existing participants extending activities and new entrants coming in.
Revenue growth was largely driven by access lines, call volumes and usage of enhanced network and cellular services.

Normalised national call revenue increased 1.6 percent while international call revenue decreased 1.2 percent reflecting a reduction in inward call revenue partially offset by increases in revenue from outward calls and other international services.
Adjusted cellular and other mobile services revenue grew by 14.8 percent.
Enhanced network services revenue increased by 32.6 percent, $21.9 million, with 0800 line revenues up strongly.
Revenues from regional directories increased by 8.3 percent.
Capital expenditure for the quarter amounted to $111.8 million, down $10.4 million, 8.5 percent.

Net cash flows from operating activities for the quarter rose by $34.9 million to $416 million due to higher receipts from customers partially offset by increased payments to suppliers and employees and increased redundancy and restructuring payments.
